summary: ARGUS-OS1 is a VitaDAO funding proposal ($100,000, 15 months) from the Georgia Longevity Alliance to investigate whether inherited centriole age predicts cell-division timing in telomerase-immortalized human fibroblasts. The project combines an open-hardware microscope (OpenFlexure-derived), on-device AI (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin), and label-free lineage tracking to run autonomous multi-week single-cell experiments. The project is self-assessed at TRL 2–3, with an open prototype V6 and a published Zenodo deposit already in place.

content_blocks.title: Project Overview and TRL Self-Assessment
content_blocks.content: ARGUS-OS1 is a VitaDAO proposal requesting $100,000 over 15 months. Applicant: Jaba Tqemaladze, MD, Georgia Longevity Alliance (Tbilisi/Abastumani, Georgia). Focus: longevity/aging biology. Self-assessed TRL: 2–3. Evidence cited for TRL: open prototype V6 exists, public GitHub repo, and a published Zenodo deposit. The project asks whether the age of the centriole a cell inherits predicts how fast it divides — a question framed as unanswerable by prior continuous measurement. Outputs are to be tokenised as an IP-NFT owned by the VitaDAO community.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale and Hypothesis
content_blocks.content:
Aging is framed as a failure of cell renewal and damage handling. The core question: does a dividing cell 'remember' which organelles it inherited, and does that memory change division rate over generations? A measurable, continuous division-rate phenotype tied to an inherited structure (centriole age) would provide a new longevity readout and a screenable endpoint for interventions (senolytics, autophagy activators, senomorphics).

Key prior literature cited:
- Spindle-size asymmetry linked to centrosome/centriole age (Thomas & Meraldi 2024, PMID 39012627)
- Asynchronous primary-cilium growth (Anderson & Stearns 2009, PMID 19682908)
- Cell-fate decisions in stem-cell systems (Reina & Gonzalez 2014, PMID 25047620; Chen & Yamashita 2021, PMID 33435817)
- Structural differences between mother and daughter centrioles (Gottardo et al. 2015, PMID 26092937)
- Centriole duplication deregulation (Nigg & Holland 2018, PMID 29363672)
- Theoretical proposal: old centrioles accumulate selectively in stem cells over time (Tkemaladze 2023, PMID 36583780)
- Open hardware for affordable long-term microscopy (openFrame, Lightley et al. 2023; OpenFlexure, Collins et al. 2020)
- Label-free lineage reconstruction from transmitted light (Waliman et al. 2024, PMID 39139100)
- Agent-driven autonomous discovery (Boiko et al. 2023; Bran et al. 2024)

Falsifiable hypothesis: In telomerase-immortalized human fibroblasts, a lineage inheriting the grandmother (oldest) centriole at each division will show a different interdivision-time trajectory from a lineage inheriting the younger mother centriole. A null result within a pre-specified window is explicitly stated as informative and will be reported.

content_blocks.title: Experimental Approach and Methods
content_blocks.content:
MODEL SYSTEMS:
- BJ-hTERT (ATCC CRL-3627) — male origin
- MRC-5 hTERT — male origin
- IMR-90-hTERT (female) — added in expanded version if resources allow
- Line identities, clones, passages, and karyotype verified before main run to separate natural crisis from centriole-age effects

CENTRIOLE-AGE ASSIGNMENT:
- OLD/NEW defined by inheritance history, not by a marker
- OLD lineage: inherits centrosome containing grandmother (oldest) centriole
- NEW lineage: inherits younger mother centriole
- Founder's first division anchors assignment (mature Cep164+ vs new Cep164−)
- Age propagated by continuous lineage tracking
- Maturation markers (Odf2/cenexin, tubulin PTMs) used as cross-check only
- Target indeterminate rate: ≤10%; below-threshold events flagged indeterminate, never auto-decided
- Classification error measured against independently scored subset

INSTRUMENT:
- OpenFlexure-derived open microscope (CERN OHL fork)
- CO₂ incubator, motorized stage, two open-source FOSH micromanipulators
- On-device AI agent on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin (275 TOPS)
- Cell segmentation: Cellpose/StarDist
- Lineage reconstruction: Kalman filter, label-free transmitted-light
- Closed-loop focus/illumination/stage control
- Lineage knowledge base with provenance to raw images
- Offline operation; raw data never leave the lab

PHOTOTOXICITY CONTROLS:
- Label-free transmitted-light channel
- Measured light budget (SNR ≥3 at minimum exposure)
- No-imaging controls: imaged cultures must retain ≥95% of control division rate and ≥90% viability over 14 days (one-sided 95% CI)
- Division-rate-trend monitoring over whole run

PRIMARY ENDPOINT AND STATISTICS:
- Difference in interdivision time between OLD and NEW lineages
- Hierarchical mixed-effect model with random intercepts per lineage nested in independent cultures and cell lines, plus sibling-pair random effect
- Alpha 0.05, power 80%
- Intra-culture correlation estimated from pilot
- Minimal detectable effect fixed before full run
- Lower bound: six independent cultures per line
- Multiplicity-controlled
- Right-censored interdivision times handled by survival-type likelihood
- Tracking loss and cell death modelled as separate event classes
- Independent biological unit: independent culture (not cell count)
- Pre-specified sensitivity analysis reclassifying OLD/NEW at extremes of indeterminate threshold
- Independent re-scoring of primary dataset subset
- Independent statistical audit

content_blocks.title: Deliverables
content_blocks.content:
All outputs are open and tokenised in the IP-NFT:
1. The method — validated centriole-age inheritance protocol (OSF preregistration, protocols.io)
2. The dataset — lineage tables + representative raw images + provenance to raw data (Zenodo DOI); target: 1,000 cells, five generations, provenance-tracked lineage tables
3. The platform — open on-device agent ('brain'), models, hardware BOM/assembly (GitHub Apache-2.0 / CERN-OHL-S)
4. The result — biological answer (positive or null) in a preprint and journal submission

Adoption targets by year 2: at least two independent laboratories running the brain on their own optics; one external re-derivation of a published lineage result from the open release alone.

Data formats: OME-TIFF (imaging), CSV/Parquet (lineage tables), OME metadata model. Retained for at least five years. Licences: Apache-2.0 (code), CERN-OHL-S (hardware), CC-BY (metadata/lineage tables).

content_blocks.content:

content_blocks.title: 15-Month Timeline
content_blocks.content:
M1–3: Build instrument V6; run brain on Jetson in real time; fine-tune segmentation on markers; calibrate micromanipulators; baseline gates (SNR ≥3, precision/recall ≥0.85, identity preservation ≥95% over 10 generations).

M2–4: Stable lines with markers; phototoxicity non-inferiority gate; centriole-age validation against independent ground-truth set.

M5–9: 500-cell pilot; power estimate; autonomy metrics (uptime, recovery, lineage loss, contamination, emergency-stop).

M10–13: Full run at pre-specified n; secondary exploratory damage arms with sham controls.

M13–15: Analysis, independent review, release (dataset, models, brain, hardware), preprint + journal submission.

content_blocks.title: Risk Register
content_blocks.content:
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| OLD/NEW misclassification | Inheritance-history definition, independent ground-truth, indeterminate ≤10% |
| Phototoxicity over months | Label-free channel, light budget, no-imaging controls, trend monitoring |
| Lineage identity loss | Identity-preservation gate ≥95% over 10 generations |
| Long-term autonomy | Autonomy metrics + emergency-stop + defined human touchpoints |
| Single-programmer dependency | Code reviews, open development, external technical review at M6 |
| Import/customs delay | Contingency line, alternative suppliers |
| Null biological result | Informative; platform/dataset/method still delivered |
| Statistical sensitivity | Pre-specified sensitivity analysis; independent re-scoring; independent statistical audit |

content_blocks.content:

content_blocks.title: IP and Open Science Framework
content_blocks.content:
IP-NFT tokenises: (1) validated centriole-age inheritance protocol; (2) lineage tables and representative raw data with provenance; (3) open on-device agent, models, and hardware designs. IP-NFT holders participate in governance of the resulting research asset. Scientific publications remain open and unencumbered.

All outputs released under: Apache-2.0 (code), CERN-OHL-S (hardware), CC-BY (metadata and lineage tables). CC-BY-NC only if a funder requires it.

AI disclosure: generative AI used in drafting the proposal (prompt log available on request); the project itself uses established computer-vision models (Cellpose, StarDist) — machine learning, not generative AI.

content_blocks.title: Current Development Status (TRL Evidence)
content_blocks.content:
Self-assessed TRL: 2–3.

Evidence for current TRL:
- Open prototype V6 exists (instrument hardware)
- Public GitHub repository
- Published Zenodo deposit
- No experimental results from the proposed study are yet available (study not yet started)
- The proposal is entirely prospective; all experimental data (pilot, full run) are planned
- Prior theoretical work by Tkemaladze 2023 (PMID 36583780) provides conceptual basis
- No cell-line experiments, no lineage tracking results, no division-time data reported in this document

The project is at the concept/early prototype stage: the instrument platform is partially built (V6 prototype), but the biological experiment has not been conducted. TRL 2–3 is consistent with the evidence presented.

key_findings: Self-assessed TRL 2–3: open instrument prototype V6 exists with public GitHub repo and Zenodo deposit, but no biological experimental results are yet available.

Core hypothesis (falsifiable): lineages inheriting the grandmother (oldest) centriole will show different interdivision-time trajectories vs. lineages inheriting the younger mother centriole, in telomerase-immortalized human fibroblasts (BJ-hTERT, MRC-5 hTERT).
No prior study has demonstrated an effect of inherited centriole age on division timing across many generations — this is a novel, unanswered question.
Model systems: BJ-hTERT (ATCC CRL-3627) and MRC-5 hTERT (both male origin); IMR-90-hTERT (female) added if resources allow.
Centriole-age assignment is inheritance-history based (not marker-based); Cep164+/− anchors founder division; indeterminate rate target ≤10%.

Instrument: OpenFlexure-derived open microscope with on-device AI (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, 275 TOPS), Cellpose/StarDist segmentation, Kalman-filter lineage tracking, label-free transmitted-light imaging.
Phototoxicity controls: ≥95% control division rate and ≥90% viability over 14 days (one-sided 95% CI) required for no-imaging controls.
Statistical plan: hierarchical mixed-effect model, alpha 0.05, power 80%, ≥6 independent cultures per line, survival-type likelihood for right-censored interdivision times, pre-registered.
Target dataset: 1,000 cells, five generations, provenance-tracked lineage tables.
Budget: $100,000 total; largest cost is AI/compute hardware ($38,409); biology/instrument $17,900; team $25,200; PI takes no salary.
No active funding at time of submission; three pending grants (Foresight Institute $100K, NLnet €23K, Open Science Collective $17K).
All outputs (method, dataset, platform, result) to be released open-source and tokenised as IP-NFT owned by VitaDAO community.
Platform designed to generalize to organoids and organs-on-chip; commercial live-cell systems cost $15,000–$50,000 vs. <$10,000 for this open instrument.
Null result is explicitly pre-specified as informative and will be reported; platform/dataset/method delivered regardless of biological outcome.
Team is small (PI + AI programmer + hardware engineer + advisor); single-programmer dependency is a stated risk with procedural mitigation.
